findings: src/optimizer/join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp: dropping RIGHT_SEMI/RIGHT_ANTI from the bail-out is sound. Both join types output only build rows. Each pushed filter (min/max, BF) is built from one condition's build-side keys, so a probe row it rejects cannot satisfy that condition for any build row and can never match. Removing it changes neither the SEMI nor the ANTI output, inequality conditions included. NOT_DISTINCT_FROM conditions are still skipped.

src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp SelectionIsReplaceableByJoinFilter: the guards are structural, not workload-specific: a SEMI delim join, one DelimGet, a single INNER/SEMI join with only `=` conditions between column refs, and an RHS of only proj/filter/get/INNER-SEMI joins. This describes a natural class: correlated EXISTS with equality correlation. Removing the DelimGet join is the same rewrite the existing code already applies when HasSelection is false, so the only new decision is plan choice.

src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp NOT DISTINCT FROM → `=` rewrite: RemoveJoinWithDelimGet adds IS NOT NULL on other_side for every COMPARE_EQUAL condition, and the guard requires all conditions to be COMPARE_EQUAL. So every binding in non_null_bindings is non-null above that filter. The RHS subtree may only contain INNER/SEMI joins, so nothing NULL-extends those columns further up. Projections are followed only through plain column refs. For a SEMI join with a non-null RHS key, a NULL LHS key gives false under both NDF and `=`, so the result is unchanged.
Minor: HasSelection(delim_join) is evaluated twice, and a forward declaration of OperatorIsDelimGet was added. This is cosmetic and not a reason to reject.
The author did not run the sqllogictests. The hand-built NULL checks (EXISTS, NOT EXISTS and IN with NULLs on both sides) cover the semantic edge I would have checked.
